title: Reduce GPU memory & workspace for inference: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, and arena tuning
description:
Context: Several production workloads reported OOMs and high GPU memory footprints when running long-context generation end-to-end. This PR reduces peak device memory and transient workspace by enabling selective activation checkpointing for attention/FFN kernels, switching to a smaller scratch buffer strategy for fused-kernel paths, and tuning the memory arena allocator thresholds to avoid oversized temporary allocations. The changes are opt-in behind runtime flags and conservative by default; we enable them for our internal perf-canary profiles to validate regressions.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a selective activation checkpointing pass that checkpoints activations for large MLP and attention blocks only when sequence_length * hidden_dim crosses a heuristic threshold. This reduces peak activation memory while keeping recompute overhead bounded. 2) Reworks GPU scratch buffer allocation to prefer per-stream pooled small buffers (4–64KB) and a single large fallback buffer rather than many transient allocations per kernel call. 3) Introduces arena tuning knobs and a heuristic to cap arena fragmentation: max_slot_size, compact_on_free_pct, and fallback_split_threshold. 4) Exposes runtime flags and a canary profile: --mem-reduce-enabled, --arena-compact-pct, --scratch-mode=pooled|legacy. 5) Adds metrics (runtime.mem.peak, runtime.mem.scratch_allocs, runtime.arena.frag_pct) and alerts for >15% regression against baseline.

Commits summary: - 7f3d2a4: add selective activation checkpointing + unit tests - 9c1b8e2: implement pooled scratch buffers + integration tests - a45f0c1: arena tuning knobs + telemetry - 2b4e9f0: default flag wiring and perf-canary profile

Files changed (high level): src/runtime/gpu/memory_arena.rs, src/runtime/gpu/scratch_pool.rs, src/runtime/optimizations/activation_checkpointing.rs, tests/integration/mem_regression.rs, infra/perf-canary/profiles/mem-reduce.yml

Testing: unit tests for checkpointing correctness and scratch allocator behavior added. Integration perf-canary runs show ~18-26% reduction in peak GPU resident memory on long-context summarization and 3–7% latency regression at 2–5 token/s workloads due to recompute; overall cost/sec reduced for throughput workloads. CI: full-test, lint, and perf-canary ran.

Backward compat and rollout: Flags default to off for public tenants. We enable for internal canary and specific Dedicated clusters. Rollout checklist included. Related Linear: ENG-1429, ENG-1782.

Motivation and tradeoffs: Activation checkpointing trades compute for memory. We added heuristics to avoid regressing short-context latency. Arena tuning reduces fragmentation but requires careful defaults per GPU family. The scratch pooling reduces many cudaMalloc/cudaFree calls that were causing memory metadata overhead in high-concurrency scenarios.

Please review the memory semantics in memory_arena.rs and the checkpoint placement heuristics in activation_checkpointing.rs. TODO: follow-up to add per-model tuned thresholds and GPU-family defaults.
